opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jason Hansen (employee ID E044) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E044.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Jason Hansen (E044) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Payroll. Full-time employees can be granted up to write; admin requires that the employee's role owns the system, and Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Requested access exceeds the allowed level, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jason Hansen (E044) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend granting read for Payroll.
reason: Jason Hansen (E044) requested admin access to Payroll. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR states full_time Engineer (max write; admin not allowed since Engineer does not own Payroll), while Security states contractor with basic training (max read; write requires advanced training, never admin). Because the facts conflict and admin is above either maximum, I grant the most restrictive level that is valid under both interpretations: read.
